title: The Possessive 'S (Apostrophe S)
description: Show who owns what using apostrophe s ('s) for singular and plural nouns.
objectives: Attach 's to singular nouns to indicate possession (Ali's car, the teacher's desk)
Add only an apostrophe (') to regular plural nouns ending in -s (the students' books)
Attach 's to irregular plural nouns that do not end in -s (the children's toys, women's rights)

sections.title: Rules for Possessive Apostrophe S
sections.content:
To show that something belongs to a person or animal, English adds an **apostrophe + s ('s)**.

### The Three Rules of Possessive S
1. **Singular nouns**: Add **'s** (*Ali's book*, *the teacher's desk*, *the cat's tail*).
2. **Regular plural nouns ending in -s**: Add **only an apostrophe (')** after the s (*the students' exam results*, *the teachers' lounge*).
3. **Irregular plural nouns NOT ending in -s**: Add **'s** (*the children's room*, *the men's suits*, *the people's choice*).

callouts.title: Its vs. It's
callouts.text: **It's** with an apostrophe ALWAYS means *It is* or *It has*. The possessive pronoun **its** NEVER has an apostrophe (*The dog wagged **its** tail*).

callouts.title: Plural vs Possessive
callouts.text: Do NOT use an apostrophe to make a word plural! Say *two dogs* (plural), NOT *two dog's*.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: Singular nouns add 's (Ali's book, the teacher's pen).
Regular plural nouns ending in -s add only an apostrophe (') (the students' marks).
Irregular plurals without -s add 's (the children's toys, women's college).
Never use an apostrophe for regular plurals (two dogs, NOT two dog's).
Remember: It's = It is; Its = belonging to it.
